narrative.title: The Rescue Helioload
narrative.scenario: A rescue helicopter has a strict cargo capacity W, and ground crews have queued up crates, each with a weight and a mission-critical value score. The chopper can lift a crate only whole — no partial loads. The mission planner must choose which crates fly so the rescued value is as high as possible without busting the lift limit.
narrative.inputFormat: Integers n and W, plus arrays wt and val of length n holding each crate's weight and value.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the maximum total value achievable with total weight at most W, taking each crate at most once.

testCases.explanation: Only the third crate fits (weight 1), scoring 3; any heavier crate alone is worth less.
Crates weighing 3 and 4 load together for 20 + 30 = 50 at exactly the weight cap.

hintLevels: Level 1: Each crate is a binary decision — load it if the remaining capacity allows, else skip.
Level 2: best[i][w] = max(best[i-1][w], val[i] + best[i-1][w - wt[i]]) with the take branch guarded by capacity.
Level 3: Sweep capacity right-to-left over a 1D array so the take branch reads the previous item's row.
